title: Knuth's root window is exact for concave nondecreasing length weights
statement: Let N ≥ 1 and h: {1..N} → ℝ be concave and nondecreasing, 1 ≤ n ≤ N, and w(i,j) = h(j−i). For the interval recurrence c(i,i) = 0, c(i,j) = w(i,j) + min_{i<k≤j} [c(i,k−1) + c(k,j)], Knuth's restricted run (K(i,i) = i; minimise only over max(K(i,j−1), i+1) ≤ k ≤ min(K(i+1,j), j); K(i,j) = the chosen minimiser) is exact for every interval under the largest-minimiser tie rule and under the smallest-minimiser tie rule. With d = j − i, the chosen roots are K(i,j) = i + 1 + τ*(d) (largest rule) and K(i,j) = i + 1 + min(HR(d), Q − 1) (smallest rule), where τ*(d) = d − 1 − min(HR(d), Q − 1), HR(d) is the number of keys in the right subtree of the heap-shaped (complete, array-layout) tree with d keys, Q = 2^⌊log₂ k_max⌋, and k_max is the largest j ∈ {2..N} with h(j) > h(j−1) (k_max = 1 if h is constant). The value τ*(d) does not depend on N ≥ d, so the statement extends to concave nondecreasing h on {1, 2, ...} and every n.
